confident: Confident and assertive: direct statements, active voice, no filler hedging (I think, maybe, possibly) or unnecessary apologies, while staying respectful. Keep any real uncertainty or condition about facts.
sales: Sales or outreach: lead with the value to the reader, keep it brief and specific, and end with the text's own request or question as a clear, low-effort call to action. No hype, exaggeration or new offers.
feedback: Performance feedback or an improvement plan: fair, specific and non-judgmental. Describe the observed behaviour, its impact if the text gives it, the expectation, and any support the text offers. About actions, never personality.
apology: A sincere apology: acknowledge what happened and its impact, take responsibility without excuses, and say what will be done to fix or prevent it if the text says so.
complaint: Customer complaint. If the text replies to a customer: empathetic, accountable and focused on the solution and the next steps the text gives. If the writer is complaining: firm, factual and polite, stating the problem, its impact and the remedy wanted.
